brief.topic: Stillness Made from Two Moving Waves

s01: Some places on a vibrating string can stay still.
That stillness can come from two waves traveling in opposite directions.
Separate their mathematical contributions for a moment.
The upper wave travels right, and the lower one travels left.
They have equal amplitude and wavelength.
The actual displacement is their sum.
At this marked place, one contribution is up while the other is equally down.
As time passes, this point stays still.
Between the nodes, the contributions can reinforce each other.
The string moves up and down, but the pattern does not travel sideways.
The distance between neighboring nodes is half a wavelength.
Use waves with half the wavelength.
More still points now fit into the same space.
This is an ideal model of waves adding together, shown slowly.
A quiet point need not mean nothing is happening; it can be where two movements meet.

scenes.narration:
Some places on a vibrating string can stay still. That stillness can come from two waves traveling in opposite directions.

Separate their mathematical contributions for a moment. The upper wave travels right, and the lower one travels left. They have equal amplitude and wavelength. The actual displacement is their sum.

At this marked place, one contribution is up while the other is equally down. They cancel. As time passes, this point stays still. It is called a node.

Between the nodes, the contributions can reinforce each other. The string moves up and down, but the pattern does not travel sideways. The distance between neighboring nodes is half a wavelength.

Use waves with half the wavelength. More still points now fit into the same space. This is an ideal model of waves adding together, shown slowly. A quiet point need not mean nothing is happening; it can be where two movements meet.
